input.quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer.
input.rationale: The IP architecture is otherwise aligned with our preferred position: 14.1 keeps all Customer Data and Customer IP with us with only a limited processing right to Vendor (reinforced by 15.1's no-sale/no-model-training limits), 14.3 leaves Vendor Technology with Vendor but pulls in the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence in 13.2 for anything embedded in or required to use a Deliverable, and 14.4 bars joint ownership and protects our feedback. The single deviation is in 14.2: ownership of Deliverables is expressed as vesting "upon creation" yet is simultaneously made "subject to payment of the applicable Fees", which is internally inconsistent and would let a fee dispute (even over unrelated or disputed amounts) defeat our title to work product we commissioned. We removed the payment condition so title vests on creation; Vendor retains its payment remedies, including the suspension right in 13.3. Fallback if pushed: condition vesting only on payment of undisputed Fees for the specific Deliverable.

ops.oldText: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer.
ops.newText: Upon creation, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer, and such ownership is not conditioned on payment of Fees.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the payment condition so title to Deliverables vests in us on creation, consistent with our position that we own what we pay for and that ownership is not held hostage to a fee dispute; Vendor retains its usual payment remedies (including suspension under Section 13.3). If Vendor needs a payment link, we could accept vesting conditioned only on payment of undisputed Fees for the relevant Deliverable.
proposal.summary: Deliverable ownership vests on creation, not subject to payment of Fees.
